observation: Measurement discipline caught spec mismatch early: spec framed AF2 as 'mostly test-strictness' (~286 errors), but fresh measurement showed only 99 of ~285 errors were test index-access. Architecture plan re-measured all seven packages under the real gate (tsc --noEmit filtered) and built the policy decision on accurate counts (shared 155 own-errors, distributed 91 test-index-access + 30 src-index-access + 34 config/genuine), not spec assumption. Cost: one pre-planning re-measure round was worth it — the mischaracterization would have cost downstream policy rework.

Stray build artifacts (tsc -b or equivalent) emitted .js/.d.ts files into src/ directories mid-implementation, which Biome then linted as 216 errors and initially misreported as pre-existing baseline. Root cause: a builder environment step ran tsc in build-mode instead of --noEmit. Cost: full cleanup commit + re-verify cycle + Biome config gate (noNonNullAssertion off only for test-file ranges) to prevent it cascading. Lesson: AF2-type workpackages must use tsc --noEmit exclusively; build mode has no place in a type-fix workpackage.

Binding test-strictness policy (fix-all-call-sites, never relax noUncheckedIndexedAccess) now propagates to AF3-AF5, with unknown cascade cost. Server has ~3780 errors; if a large share are test index-access under the same policy, that's potentially several-hundred mechanical !-assertion / narrow edits inherited by AF4. The decision is sound (the alternative un-checks tests forever), but AF4 estimate should size this cost honestly rather than wave the inherited burden through.

Cast discipline enforced via review: builder initially introduced multiple `as unknown as T` casts (forbidden by contract), which a review round eliminated entirely except one @lore-justified JSX bridge in require-ds-attribute.ts. The contrast between initial (5+ as-unknown casts) and final (1, documented) shows the contract gate worked. All remaining `as` casts are named-type, sound, and either guarded by invariants or documented with @lore.

Clean per-package drain discipline: 7 commits (one per package) each with a simultaneous tsconfig fix, code fix, and debt.json drain entry deletion. Gate remains green at each step (stale-ratchet enforces non-excepted packages must have zero errors). No batch drains; no clearing without immediate drain; no post-hoc cleanup.

Architecture critique (8.4/10) caught the getFilename characterization error before implementation and correctly flagged it UNVERIFIED. Critique: plan said 'rename getFilename() to filename', but the actual code already reads `context.filename ?? context.getFilename()` at all 7 sites. Real fix: delete the dead fallback. Builder followed the UNVERIFIED flagging discipline and the critique finding was applied (fallback deleted, not renamed). Multi-phase review caught what initial reading would have missed.

No runtime behavior change except guarded genuine-bug fixes: all 77 file changes were type-level or non-emitting (ssrf guards, derive-blocks index guards, schema type narrowing). Golden-ids snapshot test proves derive output unchanged. Integration tests green. The workpackage respected the contract: type-only tooling fix, zero behavior delta.
